However, despite this progress, current approaches still struggle to surpass human performance on tasks that require long-term memo...

evidence.excerpt:
We introduce TT-MBRL, a novel learning framework for MBRL that takes advantage of test-time
observations to learn episode-specific patterns and acquire long-term memory. TT-MBRL learns
a unique world model and policy for each evaluation episode. In contrast to training time, where
model parameters are shared across all episodes in the replay buffer, this allows the agent to fine-
tune its parameters to each individual episode. An overview of the proposed method is provided in
Figure 3.
Figure 3: During training, the world model learns to predict the common patterns shared among
multiple episode trajectories collected during exploration. The agent can solely rely on contextual
memory to identify patterns that are unique to each new episode, which can lead to incoherent future
predictions. At test time, the agent can leverage both contextual and neural memory. This allows the

At test time, the agent initializes test-time network parameters (ϕ ′,θ ′,ψ ′) with the set of weights
learned during the training phase (ϕ,θ,ψ) at the beginning of each episode. A dedicated test-time
replay buffer is also created to store observations collected within the current evaluation episode.
Analogous to the training procedure, the agent samples mini-batches of trajectories to update its
parameters. We find it beneficial to draw half of the trajectories from the training replay buffer and
the other half from the test-time buffer. This strategy acts as a form of regularization, mitigating
overfitting to the limited test-time observations, which could otherwise degrade performance. When
the number of test-time samples is smaller than the required world model sequence length, mini-
batches are concatenated with trajectories from the training buffer. We also freeze the encoder

evidence.excerpt:
introduces
a trade-off, as it delays the benefits of adaptation. To overcome both limitations, we propose mixing
trajectories collected at test time with samples from the training replay buffer (Test+Train Data, No
Prefill), effectively acting as a form of regularization. This approach mitigates early overfitting while
enabling immediate adaptation, leading to more stable and consistent performance improvements.
To verify that the gain in performance is due to TT-MBRL rather than additional inference compute,
we also perform a compute-matched evaluation. We study the impact of additional compute on per-
formance when only training trajectories are available (Train Data Only). The comparison confirms
that the performance gain is due to TT-MBRL rather than additional compute budget.
Table 5: Impact of replay buffer sampling strategy on TT-MBRL performance on Memory Maze

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Episode reward measured directly in the environment and ground-truth video-quality metrics (FVD, PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS) corroborate the test-time gains independently of the test-time optimization loss.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Ground-truth environment returns and video prediction metrics computed against real trajectories.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: World model reconstruction/KL/reward/continuation losses plus actor-critic imagined-return maximization during test-time adaptation.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported performance metrics directly corroborate the claims that test-time parameter adaptation provides effective episode-specific memory and enhances long-horizon planning in partially observable environments.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluations are rigorous across DreamerV3, TWISTER, and R2I backbones on both Memory Maze 2D and the 3D Memory Maze benchmark, showing substantial task return improvements and consistent reductions in world model prediction errors (KL divergence, FVD, PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS). Thorough ablation studies control for test-time compute matching, buffer mixing ratios, gradient frequencies, and confirm no regression on standard benchmarks (DeepMind Control Suite, Atari 100k).

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Task reward accumulation in the environment and independent video quality metrics evaluate agent behavior without circular dependence on the test-time loss.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Objective environment episode returns (cumulative task rewards) and standard video quality metrics (FVD, PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS) computed against ground-truth environment trajectories.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: World model self-supervised loss (KL divergence and reward/continuation prediction) and policy RL return maximization on imagined rollouts during training and test episodes.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly discuss and quantify the computational overhead of performing gradient-based optimization during evaluation episodes, as well as the need for exploration-phase adaptations in future work.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is clearly defined, presenting the test-time optimization objectives, replay buffer mixing (50/50 train/test sampling) to mitigate overfitting, and encoder/decoder parameter freezing to preserve latent representation spaces while reducing computation. Complete algorithm pseudocode, architectural details, and hyperparameters are fully reported.
primary.quality_rationale: The work addresses a clear limitation in model-based RL through a principled, well-ablated approach. The evaluation is comprehensive across multiple baselines and environments, supported by compute-matched controls and external benchmark validations.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces Test-Time Model-Based Reinforcement Learning (TT-MBRL), which adapts world model and actor-critic parameters online during test episodes using a mixture of test-time observations and replay buffer data without updating visual encoder/decoder weights, enhancing long-term episodic memory across multiple world-model backbones.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The work addresses a clear limitation in model-based RL through a principled, well-ablated approach. The evaluation is comprehensive across multiple baselines and environments, supported by compute-matched controls and external benchmark validations.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors explicitly discuss and quantify the computational overhead of performing gradient-based optimization during evaluation episodes, as well as the need for exploration-phase adaptations in future work.
